articles.heading: Scope & Key Requirements (Public Summary)
articles.text: Requires firms to design, implement, and operate a risk-based system of quality management (SOQM) covering governance, ethics, acceptance/continuance, engagement performance, resources, information/communication, and monitoring/remediation.

articles.heading: Eight Components of Firm Quality Management (SOQM)
articles.text:
Requires firms to design and operate a proactive, risk-based System of Quality Management (SOQM) covering 8 integrated components:
• (1) Firm's risk assessment process (quality objectives → quality risks → responses); (2) Governance and leadership; (3) Relevant ethical requirements; (4) Acceptance and continuance of client relationships; (5) Engagement performance; (6) Resources (human, technological, intellectual); (7) Information and communication; (8) Monitoring and remediation process.
• Annual evaluation (ISQM 1.53–55): leadership must evaluate at least annually whether the SOQM provides reasonable assurance that its objectives are being achieved (converged with China QMS 5101).

articles.text: Deals with the auditor's responsibilities relating to fraud in an audit of financial statements, including reinforced professional skepticism, fraud risk identification, and transparent communication (Revised July 2025).

articles.heading: Fraud Responsibilities, Presumed Risks & 2025 Revision Highlights
articles.text:
• Fraud triangle & skepticism (ISA 240.12–16): maintain heightened professional skepticism throughout; hold mandatory engagement team discussion on fraud susceptibility.
• Two presumed fraud risks (ISA 240.27, 32): (1) improper revenue recognition (rebuttable, must document if rebutted); (2) management override of controls (NEVER rebuttable — mandatory journal entry testing, retrospective review of estimates, and evaluation of significant unusual transactions).
• July 2025 Revised Edition highlights: clarifies auditor's role on fraud, reinforces fraud-lens risk assessment aligned with ISA 315, strengthens responses when fraud or suspected fraud is identified, and enhances transparency in auditor's reports (converged with China CSA 1141).

articles.heading: Scope & Key Requirements (Public Summary)
articles.text: Deals with the auditor's responsibility to identify and assess the risks of material misstatement in the financial statements through understanding the entity, its environment, and its system of internal control.

articles.heading: Spectrum of Inherent Risk, Significant Risks & ITGCs
articles.text:
• Risk identification & assessment (ISA 315.19–34): separately assess Inherent Risk (using 5 inherent risk factors: complexity, subjectivity, change, uncertainty, susceptibility to bias/fraud) and Control Risk.
• Significant risk (ISA 315.12(l), 32): an identified risk of material misstatement where inherent risk sits close to the upper end of the spectrum of inherent risk (triggers mandatory substantive responses under ISA 330).
• IT environment & ITGCs (ISA 315.26, Appendix 5): identify risks arising from use of IT and evaluate design & implementation of General IT Controls (ITGCs) addressing those risks (converged with China CSA 1211).

articles.heading: Sufficient Appropriate Audit Evidence & Reliability Hierarchy
articles.text:
• Sufficiency (quantity) and Appropriateness (quality = relevance + reliability) (ISA 500.6, A4–A5).
• Reliability principles (ISA 500.A31): independent external sources > internal records; effective controls increase internal reliability; direct auditor-obtained evidence > indirect; documentary > oral; originals > photocopies.
